mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 2% over the prior 3 months reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing near-term S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.5% over the last 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS increase, or IC > 0.05 over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS indicates labor market strength that supports corporate earnings growth and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by 2% from the prior month
failure_condition: IC < -0.1 over 60-day window or SPX 20-day returns negative during PAYEMS up periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (GDPC1) suggests weakening aggregate demand, which lowers growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns within 5 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by 4% from the prior quarter
failure_condition: 20-day returns positive despite GDPC1 decline, or IC > 0.2 over 5-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Industrial Production index (INDPRO) below 95 suggests supply-side softness that reduces growth prospects and drives negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: IC < 0.05 over 20-day window or returns positive when INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month CPIAUCSL inflation rate crosses above 2%, the market anticipates future rate hikes, which compresses discount rates and produces negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by 0.4 percentage points from prior month
failure_condition: 20-day returns positive with CPIAUCSL above 2% or IC > 0.1 over horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) suggests weakening labor demand and triggers a 5-day negative S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates earnings pressure.
failure_condition: 20-day returns positive during PAYEMS spike or IC > 0.2 over 5-day window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both industrial production (GDPC1) and consumer demand (HOUST) create a supply-demand imbalance that produces positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as the market anticipates profit expansion.
regime_hint: dual softness in supply and demand
failure_condition: IC < 0.05 for GDPC1 and HOUST, or 20-day returns negative despite both declines.

mechanism_narrative: During a post-2008 financial crisis recovery regime, a rise in consumer confidence (not directly observable here) is expected to translate into stronger equity valuations, producing positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns negative when CPIAUCSL shows upward momentum, or IC < -0.2 over window.
